questions.question:
Triangle PQR has PQ = 5, PR = 8 and angle QPR = a degrees. Triangle STU has ST = 5, SU = 8 and angle TSU = b degrees. It is given that 90 < a < b < 180.
Quantity A: The area of triangle PQR
Quantity B: The area of triangle STU
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
questions.explanation:
1. Put the side of length 8 along a horizontal line with the enclosed angle at its left end, and let the side of length 5 run from that same end. The area is (1/2) x 8 x h, where h is the height of the far end of the 5-side above that line.
2. As the enclosed angle grows from 90 degrees toward 180 degrees, the 5-side swings down toward the line, so h shrinks: at 90 degrees h is the full 5, and at 180 degrees h is 0 and the triangle collapses.
3. Both angles lie between 90 and 180 degrees with a < b, so the first triangle has the greater height and therefore the greater area.
4. Check with two cases: at 120 degrees the 5-side makes a 60 degree angle with the line, so h = 5*(sqrt(3)/2), about 4.33, and the area is about 17.3; at 150 degrees the 5-side makes a 30 degree angle with the line, so h = 5*(1/2) = 2.5 and the area is 10. The smaller angle gives the larger area.
Quantity A is greater.
questions.trap: Applying the acute-angle intuition that a larger included angle always gives a larger area, so the larger angle b seems to give Quantity B the bigger area, choice B.

questions.question:
Point P = (a, 0) where a > 0, and point Q = (0, a).

Quantity A: The distance from P to the origin
Quantity B: The distance from P to Q
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
questions.explanation: Quantity A: Distance from P = (a, 0) to origin = √(a²+0) = a. Quantity B: PQ = √((0−a)²+(a−0)²) = √(2a²) = a√2. Since a > 0, a√2 > a. Quantity B is greater.
questions.trap: Students think both distances equal a and select C. The distance PQ spans both horizontal and vertical gaps, yielding a√2 ≈ 1.41a, which exceeds a.

questions.question:
A square with side 4 is inscribed in Circle A. A circle with radius 4 is inscribed in Square B.
Quantity A: Area of Circle A
Quantity B: Area of Square B
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
questions.explanation: Circle A: square side = 4, diagonal = 4√2, diameter = 4√2, radius = 2√2. Area of Circle A = π(2√2)² = 8π ≈ 25.1. Square B: circle radius = 4, so diameter = 8 = side of square. Area of Square B = 8² = 64. Since 64 > 25.1, Quantity B is greater.
questions.trap: Students confuse the two configurations. In Circle A, side = 4 means the diagonal (not the side) = diameter. In Square B, radius = 4 means diameter = 8 = side of square.

questions.question:
Circle has radius 5. Chord A is at distance 3 from the center. Chord B is at distance 4 from the center.
Quantity A: Length of Chord A
Quantity B: Length of Chord B
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
questions.explanation: For Chord A (distance 3): half-chord = √(5² - 3²) = √(25-9) = √16 = 4. Chord A = 8. For Chord B (distance 4): half-chord = √(5² - 4²) = √(25-16) = √9 = 3. Chord B = 6. Quantity A (8) > Quantity B (6).
questions.trap: Students may reason that a greater distance from the center means a longer chord (backwards). In fact, chords closer to the center are longer — the chord at distance 3 is longer than the chord at distance 4.

questions.question:
Use the following data for this question.

SET 2 — WESTFIELD UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT: Enrollment & Graduation

The Line Graph shows total student enrollment across all grades, in thousands of students, for the years 2018 through 2023. The Pie Chart breaks down the 2023 enrollment by school level, as a percentage of 2023 total enrollment; its values are listed in the table below.

According to the Line Graph, in which year was total enrollment the lowest?

A. 2018
B. 2019
C. 2020
D. 2021
E. 2022
questions.explanation:
Reading the Line Graph:
2018: 42,000 — the lowest value among all six years listed.
2019: 45,000; 2020: 43,000; 2021: 47,000; 2022: 50,000; 2023: 52,000.
The minimum is 42,000 in 2018.
questions.trap: Students notice 2020 (43,000) is lower than 2019 (45,000) and pick 2020, missing that 2018 (42,000) is even lower. Always check all data points when asked for a minimum.

questions.question:
Use the following data for this question.

SET 2 — WESTFIELD UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT: Enrollment & Graduation

The Line Graph shows total student enrollment across all grades, in thousands of students, for the years 2018 through 2023. The Pie Chart breaks down the 2023 enrollment by school level, as a percentage of 2023 total enrollment; its values are listed in the table below.

Approximately how many students were enrolled at the Middle School level in 2023?

A. 10,500
B. 12,500
C. 13,000
D. 15,600
E. 23,400
questions.explanation:
From the Line Graph, total 2023 enrollment = 52,000 students.
From the Pie Chart, Middle School = 25% of total.
Middle School enrollment = 25% × 52,000 = 0.25 × 52,000 = 13,000 students.
questions.trap: Students use 2022 enrollment (50,000) from the line graph instead of 2023 (52,000), computing 25% × 50,000 = 12,500 (option B). Always confirm which year's data the question references.

questions.question:
Use the following data for this question.

SET 2 — WESTFIELD UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT: Enrollment & Graduation

The Line Graph shows total student enrollment across all grades, in thousands of students, for the years 2018 through 2023. The Pie Chart breaks down the 2023 enrollment by school level, as a percentage of 2023 total enrollment; its values are listed in the table below.

Quantity A: Number of High School students enrolled in 2023
Quantity B: Number of Elementary students enrolled in 2021
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
questions.explanation:
Quantity A: High School in 2023 = 30% × 52,000 = 15,600 students.
Quantity B: Elementary students in 2021 — the Pie Chart only gives the 2023 breakdown. We do not have the 2021 breakdown by level. We only know total 2021 enrollment = 47,000. Without the 2021 level percentages, Quantity B cannot be determined.
Therefore, the relationship cannot be determined.
questions.trap: Students apply the 2023 pie chart percentages to 2021 enrollment, computing 45% × 47,000 = 21,150 and concluding Quantity B is greater. The pie chart percentages apply ONLY to 2023 — we cannot assume the same distribution for 2021.

questions.question: A plumber charges a flat fee of $50 for a job plus $40 for each hour of work. An electrician charges $60 for each hour of work and no flat fee. For how many hours of work do the two tradespeople charge the same total amount?
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — name the unknown. Let h = the number of hours of work.
Step 2 — translate each charge. The flat fee is paid once, not per hour.
Plumber: 50 + 40h
Electrician: 60h
Step 3 — translate 'charge the same total amount' as one equation.
50 + 40h = 60h
50 = 20h
h = 2.5
Check: plumber 50 + 40(2.5) = 50 + 100 = $150; electrician 60(2.5) = $150. Equal. Correct.
Answer: C.
questions.trap: Choice A, 0.5, comes from dividing 50 by the SUM of the two hourly rates, 40 + 60 = 100, instead of by their difference. Choice B, 1.25, comes from solving 40h = 50, ignoring the electrician entirely. Choice E, 5, comes from dividing the flat fee by 60 - 50 = 10, differencing a fee and a rate instead of the two rates. Choice D, 3, is where a student lands who insists the answer must be a whole number of hours and rounds 2.5 up; hours are a continuous quantity here, so 2.5 is a legitimate answer.

questions.question: Which of the following numbers is irrational?
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — irrational means the decimal never terminates and never repeats; equivalently, the number is not a ratio of two integers.
Step 2 — test each option.
A - -3/8 = -0.375, terminating. Rational.
B - the block 47 repeats, so 0.474747... = 47/99. Rational.
C - 22/7 is a ratio of integers by construction. Rational. (It is a famous approximation of pi, but it is not pi.)
D - 45 = 3^2 x 5, so sqrt(45) = 3 x sqrt(5). Since 5 is not a perfect square, sqrt(5) is irrational, and a non-zero rational (3) times an irrational is irrational. Irrational.
E - 49 = 7^2, so sqrt(49) = 7, an integer. Rational.
Check: the square root of a positive integer is rational only when that integer is a perfect square. 49 is; 45 is not.
Answer: D.
questions.trap: Choosing C because 22/7 is used as a stand-in for pi. A fraction of two integers is rational no matter what it approximates. Choosing B because the decimal never stops - repeating decimals are always rational.

questions.question: A municipal survey of 400 households found that 22 percent of the households owned a boat, 17 percent owned a motorcycle, and 68 percent owned neither a boat nor a motorcycle. How many of the surveyed households owned both a boat and a motorcycle?
questions.explanation:
Households owning at least one of the two = 100 - 68 = 32 percent.
32 percent of 400 = 128 households own at least one.
Boat owners = 22 percent of 400 = 88.
Motorcycle owners = 17 percent of 400 = 68.
By the two-set rule, both = boat + motorcycle - at least one = 88 + 68 - 128 = 28.
Check: boat only = 88 - 28 = 60; motorcycle only = 68 - 28 = 40; both = 28; neither = 272. Total = 60 + 40 + 28 + 272 = 400.
questions.trap: Adding the two percents and applying 39 percent to 400 without removing the overlap gives 156, option E.

questions.question:
Suppose -1 < w < 0. Consider the three values w^(1/3), w^(1/5), and 1/(w^(1/3)), where w^(1/3) is the real cube root of w and w^(1/5) is the real fifth root of w.

Which of the following statements must be true?

Indicate all such statements.
options: A. 1/(w^(1/3)) is the least of the three values.
C. w^(1/5) lies between the other two values.
E. All three of the values are negative.
questions.explanation:
Test with w = -1/8, which satisfies -1 < w < 0.
w^(1/3) = -1/2 = -0.5.
w^(1/5) = -(1/8)^(1/5) = -0.660 approximately.
1/(w^(1/3)) = 1/(-0.5) = -2.
Order from least to greatest: -2 < -0.660 < -0.5, that is 1/(w^(1/3)) < w^(1/5) < w^(1/3).
Confirm with a second value, w = -1/2: w^(1/3) = -0.794, w^(1/5) = -0.871, 1/(w^(1/3)) = -1.260. Same order.
Statement A: 1/(w^(1/3)) is least in both tests. In general, for -1 < w < 0 the cube root lies strictly between -1 and 0, so its reciprocal is below -1 and is therefore smaller than either root. True.
Statement B: w^(1/3) = -0.5 is greater than w^(1/5) = -0.660, so w^(1/3) < w^(1/5) is false.
Statement C: w^(1/5) sits between 1/(w^(1/3)) and w^(1/3) in both tests. Since an odd root of a number between -1 and 0 moves toward -1 as the index grows, the fifth root is below the cube root, and both are above -1 while the reciprocal is below -1. True.
Statement D: w^(1/3) = -0.5, which is greater than -1, so false.
Statement E: an odd root of a negative number is negative, and the reciprocal of a negative number is negative, so all three are negative. True.
Check: A, C, and E hold; B and D fail on the tested value.
questions.trap: Assuming a larger root index always produces a larger value selects B.

questions.question:
For digits a and b, write 0.abab... for the decimal whose two-digit block ab repeats forever. Let S be the total of 0.abab... over every digit pair (a, b) with a - b = 4. What is the value of S?

Give your answer as a fraction.
questions.explanation:
1. A repeating block of two digits ab equals the two-digit number divided by 99: 0.abab... = (10a + b) / 99.
2. Pairs with a - b = 4: (4,0), (5,1), (6,2), (7,3), (8,4), (9,5), giving blocks 40, 51, 62, 73, 84, 95.
3. Sum of the blocks = 40 + 51 + 62 + 73 + 84 + 95 = 405.
4. S = 405 / 99 = 45 / 11 after dividing numerator and denominator by 9.
Check: 45/11 is about 4.09, and the six decimals average about 0.68, so 6 * 0.68 is about 4.09.
questions.trap: Dividing the block sum by 100 instead of 99 (treating ab as hundredths) gives 405/100 = 81/20.

easy.question:
Quantity A: The number of positive factors of 100
Quantity B: The number of positive factors of 98
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
easy.explanation: 100 = 2² × 5², factors = (2+1)(2+1) = 9. 98 = 2 × 7² = 2¹ × 7², factors = (1+1)(2+1) = 6. Quantity A (9) > Quantity B (6). Answer is A.
easy.trap: Students may assume 100 and 98 have similar factor counts because they are close together. Proximity in value does not imply similar factor counts.

easy.question:
A cube has a surface area of 150 cm².

Quantity A: Volume of the cube
Quantity B: 125 cm³
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
easy.explanation: SA = 6s² = 150 → s² = 25 → s = 5. Volume = s³ = 5³ = 125 cm³. Quantity A = Quantity B.
easy.trap: Students compute s² = 25 and then use V = s² × s without realizing s = 5, or they make an arithmetic error. The clean numbers are intentional: SA = 150 → s = 5 → V = 125.

easy.question:
A person walks at 4 km/h for 3 hours.
Quantity A: Distance walked
Quantity B: 12 km
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
easy.trap: Students compute 4 + 3 = 7 or 4/3 ≈ 1.33. Speed × Time = Distance.

easy.question:
Points P, Q and R lie on a line, with Q between P and R. Point S does not lie on that line. Ray QM bisects angle PQS and ray QN bisects angle SQR.
Quantity A: The measure, in degrees, of angle MQN
Quantity B: 90
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
easy.explanation: Because P, Q and R are collinear with Q in the middle, angles PQS and SQR are supplementary: their measures add to 180. Ray QM lies inside angle PQS and ray QN lies inside angle SQR, so angle MQN is made up of half of angle PQS plus half of angle SQR. That is (1/2)(angle PQS + angle SQR) = (1/2)(180) = 90 degrees, no matter where S sits.
easy.trap: Students see that neither angle PQS nor angle SQR is given a value and choose 'cannot be determined'. The individual angles really are unknown, but their sum is pinned at 180 by the straight line, and only the sum of the two halves is being asked for.

easy.question:
A retailer buys an item for x dollars and sells it for y dollars, making a profit of 25 percent on cost price. He then buys a second item for y dollars and sells it at a price that gives him the same profit in DOLLARS as the first item gave him. x > 0.
Quantity A: His profit percent on cost price over the two items taken together
Quantity B: 22%
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
easy.explanation:
Step 1 — the first item: profit = 0.25*x, so y = 1.25*x.
Step 2 — the second item costs y = 1.25*x, and its profit is the same number of DOLLARS, 0.25*x. Its profit percent is therefore 0.25x/1.25x = 20 percent, lower than the first item's 25 percent, because the same dollars sit on a larger base.
Step 3 — total profit = 0.25x + 0.25x = 0.50x.
Step 4 — total cost = x + 1.25x = 2.25x.
Step 5 — combined profit percent = 0.50x/2.25x = 50/225 = 2/9 = 22.22 percent, and x cancels, so the answer does not depend on x.
Step 6 — 22.22 is greater than 22, so Quantity A is greater.
Check with x = 400: the first item costs $400 and sells for $500, a $100 profit; the second costs $500 and sells for $600, also $100. Total profit $200 on a total cost of $900, and 200/900 = 0.2222. Correct.
Answer: A.
easy.trap: Averaging the two rates as (25 + 20)/2 = 22.5 percent and then, worse, some students average to exactly 22 and answer C. A combined profit percent is total profit over TOTAL cost, a weighted average whose weights are the two cost prices; the larger cost of $1.25x pulls the result toward the 20 percent item, giving 22.22 percent rather than 22.5 percent. Answering D on the belief that x is unknown misses that x cancels.

easy.question: Which of the following is equal to x² − 14x + 49 for all values of x?
easy.explanation:
Step 1 — three terms, so look for the trinomial pattern: two numbers with product 49 and sum -14.
Step 2 — the product is positive and the sum is negative, so both numbers are negative. The pair is -7 and -7.
Step 3 — (x - 7)(x - 7) = (x - 7)^2.
Check: expand (x - 7)^2 = x^2 - 14x + 49. Correct.
Answer: A.
easy.trap: Reading the +49 as a signal for plus signs and choosing (x + 7)^2, choice B, which expands to x^2 + 14x + 49 with the wrong middle sign. Choice C is the difference-of-squares form, which would need x^2 - 49 and no middle term at all. Choice D takes the factor pair 49 and 1 without checking that the sum must be -14; it gives x^2 - 50x + 49. Choice E uses that same pair with opposite signs, as if the constant were -49; it gives x^2 - 48x - 49.

easy.question: How many three-digit positive integers are there?
easy.explanation: Three-digit integers range from 100 to 999 inclusive. Count = 999 - 100 + 1 = 900. Using the slot method: hundreds digit has 9 choices (1 through 9, not 0), tens digit has 10 choices (0 through 9), units digit has 10 choices (0 through 9): 9 x 10 x 10 = 900.
easy.trap: Students compute 10^3 = 1,000 (treating all three digits as having 10 choices each). But the hundreds digit cannot be 0 — a number like 072 is not a three-digit number. The hundreds digit has only 9 valid choices.

easy.question: The interior angle measures of convex polygon X add up to 540 degrees more than those of convex polygon Y. Polygon X has 12 sides. How many sides does polygon Y have?
easy.explanation:
Interior angle sum of an n-sided polygon = (n - 2) * 180.
For X: (12 - 2) * 180 = 1,800 degrees.
For Y: 1,800 - 540 = 1,260 degrees.
(n - 2) * 180 = 1,260 gives n - 2 = 7, so n = 9.
Check: each side lost removes 180 degrees; 540 / 180 = 3 sides fewer, and 12 - 3 = 9.
easy.trap: Taking 540/180 = 3 as the number of sides of Y instead of the number of fewer sides gives choice A; adding 3 to 12 gives 15 (choice E); dividing 540 by 90 and subtracting from 12 gives 6 (choice B).

easy.question: A store's gross margin on an item, that is, its profit as a percent of the selling price, is 40 percent. The store wants to change its markup on that item, that is, its profit as a percent of the cost price, to 100 percent, while the cost price stays the same. By what percent must the store raise the selling price?
easy.explanation:
Step 1 — translate the current margin. Profit = 0.40*SP means CP = 0.60*SP, so the current SP = CP/0.60 = (5/3)*CP.
Step 2 — translate the target markup. Profit = 1.00*CP means the target SP = CP + CP = 2*CP.
Step 3 — the required increase is measured on the current selling price: (2*CP - (5/3)*CP)/((5/3)*CP).
Step 4 — the CP cancels: (2 - 5/3)/(5/3) = (1/3)/(5/3) = 1/5 = 0.20, that is 20 percent.
Check with a number: let CP = $60. A 40 percent margin gives SP = 60/0.60 = $100, with a profit of $40 that is indeed 40 percent of $100. A 100 percent markup needs SP = $120. Raising $100 to $120 is a 20 percent increase, and the new profit of $60 is 100 percent of the $60 cost. Correct.
Answer: A.
easy.trap: Choice D, 60 percent, subtracts the two figures, 100 - 40, as though a margin and a markup were measured on the same base. Choice C, 42.86 percent, misreads the 40 percent margin as a 40 percent markup, giving a current SP of 1.4*CP and an increase of 2/1.4 - 1. Choice B, 33.33 percent, measures the increase on the COST price, (2 - 5/3)/1 = 1/3, instead of on the current selling price. Choice E assumes the selling price must double because the markup target is 100 percent.

easy.question: A survey of 50 people found that 30 like coffee and 25 like tea. If 12 people like both, how many people like neither coffee nor tea?
easy.explanation: First find those who like at least one: |Coffee ∪ Tea| = 30 + 25 - 12 = 43. Then neither = Total - at least one = 50 - 43 = 7.
easy.trap: Students forget the 'neither' group and answer 12 (the overlap) or compute 50 - 30 - 25 + 12 = 7 correctly but then second-guess themselves.

easy.question: A data set listed in increasing order is 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14. The value 14 is deleted. Using the standard method, with the median excluded from each half, how does the interquartile range change?
easy.explanation:
Step 1 — original set, 7 values. Median = 4th value = 8. Lower half {2, 4, 6} gives Q1 = 4; upper half {10, 12, 14} gives Q3 = 12. IQR = 12 - 4 = 8.
Step 2 — after deleting 14 the set is 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, an even count of 6. Split into halves of 3.
Lower half {2, 4, 6} gives Q1 = 4; upper half {8, 10, 12} gives Q3 = 10. IQR = 10 - 4 = 6.
Step 3 — the change is 6 - 8 = -2, a decrease of 2.
Answer: it decreases by 2.
easy.trap: Choosing C on the reasoning that Q3 is not the maximum, so deleting the maximum cannot touch it. Q3 is the median of the upper half, and deleting a value re-cuts the halves: the upper half slides from {10, 12, 14} to {8, 10, 12}, dragging Q3 from 12 down to 10. Choice E, a decrease of 4, comes from putting both middle values of the new 6-value set into both halves - {2, 4, 6, 8} and {6, 8, 10, 12} give Q1 = 5, Q3 = 9 and IQR = 4, so the change looks like 4 - 8 = -4. Choices A and B are those same two magnitudes with the direction reversed, from subtracting old minus new (8 - 6 = 2, or 8 - 4 = 4) and reporting the result as an increase.

easy.question:
n is a positive integer.

Which of the following values of n for the average (arithmetic mean) of n, n^2 and 1/n is greater than n + 3?

Indicate all such values.
easy.trap: Assuming the average of n, n^2 and 1/n tracks n + 3 closely and picking small values like 4 (choice C), where the average 6.75 is just short of 7.

easy.question:
The table below shows annual profit (in thousands of dollars) for a small business:
2018: $45
2019: $62
2020: $38
2021: $70
2022: $55

Which of the following years in the profit exceeded $50,000?

Select all that apply.
easy.explanation:
Check each year against the threshold of $50,000 (i.e., 50 in the table):
2018: $45K — does NOT exceed $50K
2019: $62K — exceeds $50K ✓
2020: $38K — does NOT exceed $50K
2021: $70K — exceeds $50K ✓
2022: $55K — exceeds $50K ✓
Correct answers: 2019 (B), 2021 (D), 2022 (E).
easy.trap: Students may include 2018 ($45K) thinking it is close to $50K, or misread 'exceeded' as 'at least $50K' and include a value that is exactly $50K (none exists here, but the wording matters).

easy.question: For every real number x, let floor(x) denote the largest integer that does not exceed x, and define g(x) = 3 + floor(x). What is the value of g(-2.4) + g(2.6)?
easy.explanation:
floor(-2.4) = -3, because -3 is the largest integer not exceeding -2.4 (the integer -2 is larger than -2.4).
So g(-2.4) = 3 + (-3) = 0.
floor(2.6) = 2, so g(2.6) = 3 + 2 = 5.
Sum = 0 + 5 = 5.
easy.trap: Treating floor(-2.4) as -2 (dropping the decimal part) gives g(-2.4) = 1 and a total of 6.

easy.question: On the number line A = -5 and B = 7. Point C lies on segment AB with AC : CB = 1 : 3. What is the coordinate of C?
easy.explanation:
Step 1 — total length: AB = 7 - (-5) = 12.
Step 2 — the ratio 1 : 3 splits AB into 1 + 3 = 4 equal parts, so AC is 1/4 of the whole, not 1/3.
AC = (1/4)(12) = 3.
Step 3 — walk 3 units to the RIGHT from A, since B is to the right: C = -5 + 3 = -2.
Check: CB = 7 - (-2) = 9, and AC : CB = 3 : 9 = 1 : 3. Correct.
Answer: -2.
easy.trap: Reading '1 : 3' as 'one third of the way' and taking AC = 12/3 = 4, which lands on -1. A ratio of m : n divides the segment into m + n parts, so the first piece is m/(m + n) of the total. The other slip is reversing the ratio and putting C three quarters of the way along, at -5 + 9 = 4.

medium.question:
A boat's speed in still water is 12 km/h. It travels 36 km upstream and 36 km downstream. The current's speed is c km/h, where 0 < c < 12.

Quantity A: Total time for the round trip (upstream + downstream)
Quantity B: 6 hours
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
medium.explanation: Upstream speed = 12 − c. Downstream speed = 12 + c. Time upstream = 36/(12 − c). Time downstream = 36/(12 + c). Total time = 36/(12−c) + 36/(12+c) = 36[(12+c) + (12−c)] / [(12−c)(12+c)] = 36(24) / (144−c²) = 864/(144−c²). When c = 0: total = 864/144 = 6 hours. For any c > 0: 144 − c² < 144, so 864/(144−c²) > 6. Since c > 0, Quantity A > 6 = Quantity B. Quantity A is always greater than Quantity B.
medium.trap: Students compute upstream time + downstream time as 36/12 + 36/12 = 3 + 3 = 6 hours, forgetting that the current alters the effective speeds, and choose C.

medium.question:
In the figure, triangle PQR is equilateral with each side equal to 6. Arc QSR is part of the circle with center P that passes through Q and R, and S is on the arc below chord QR.
Quantity A: The area of the region bounded by chord QR and arc QSR
Quantity B: 3
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
medium.explanation:
1. The arc is centered at P with radius PQ = 6, and angle QPR = 60 degrees (equilateral triangle).
2. The sector PQSR has area (60/360) * pi * 6^2 = 6*pi.
3. The triangle PQR has area (sqrt(3)/4) * 6^2 = 9*sqrt(3).
4. The region in Quantity A is the sector minus the triangle: 6*pi - 9*sqrt(3).
5. Numerically 6*pi is about 18.850 and 9*sqrt(3) is about 15.588, so the region is about 3.26, which is more than 3.
6. Safe bounds: 6*3.14 = 18.84 and 9*1.7321 = 15.589, giving 3.25 even with the pessimistic values. Quantity A is greater.
medium.trap: Rounding too coarsely, with pi as 3 and sqrt(3) as 1.7, gives 18 - 15.3 = 2.7, which seems to make Quantity B greater, choice B; the true value is only about 0.26 above 3, so the approximations must be tight.

medium.question:
Two chords AB and CD intersect inside a circle. AB = 12 and CD = 13. The chord AB is bisected at the intersection point.

Quantity A: The length of the longer segment of CD
Quantity B: 9
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
medium.explanation: By the intersecting-chords theorem, the product of AB's segments equals the product of CD's. AB is bisected, so each half = 6, giving 6 × 6 = 36. If CD's segments are x and 13 − x, then x(13 − x) = 36 → x² − 13x + 36 = 0 → x = 4 or 9. The longer segment is 9. Quantity A = 9 = Quantity B, so the quantities are equal.
medium.trap: Not applying the intersecting chords theorem and instead guessing the longer segment is half of CD = 6.5.

medium.question:
x is a negative number.
Quantity A: x
Quantity B: x^2
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
medium.explanation:
Step 1 — locate each column relative to zero. x is negative, so Quantity A < 0. A square of a non-zero number is positive, so Quantity B > 0.
Step 2 — anything negative is left of anything positive on the number line, so x < x^2 for EVERY negative x.
Step 3 — sample all of the negative territory to be sure:
x = -5: Quantity A = -5, Quantity B = 25. B greater.
x = -1: Quantity A = -1, Quantity B = 1. B greater.
x = -0.5: Quantity A = -0.5, Quantity B = 0.25. B greater.
x = -0.001: Quantity A = -0.001, Quantity B = 0.000001. B greater.
Quantity B is greater in every case.
Answer: B.
medium.trap: Choosing D because squaring behaves differently on x < -1 (it enlarges the magnitude) than on -1 < x < 0 (it shrinks it). That difference is real but irrelevant here: whatever the magnitude does, the sign flips to positive, and a positive always beats a negative. Never key D just because the magnitudes vary - check whether the ORDER varies.

medium.question:
M, p and q are positive numbers.
Quantity A: M(p^2 + q^2)/15
Quantity B: M(p + q)^2/15
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
medium.explanation: Both columns carry the same positive factor M/15, so the comparison reduces to p^2 + q^2 against (p + q)^2. Expanding the square gives (p + q)^2 = p^2 + 2pq + q^2, which exceeds p^2 + q^2 by exactly 2pq. Since p and q are both positive, 2pq is positive, so Quantity B is greater for every allowed choice of M, p and q.
medium.trap: Students recall that squaring a sum is not the sum of squares but cannot pin the direction, and answer 'cannot be determined'. The positivity of p and q fixes the sign of the 2pq gap, which settles it.

medium.question: In the figure, XY is a diameter of a circle whose radius is 12, and Z is a point on the circle above XY. The angle between chords XY and XZ at X measures 30 degrees. What is the length of the arc from Z to X that does not pass through Y?
medium.explanation:
Angle YXZ is an inscribed angle, so it is half of the arc it cuts off: arc YZ = 2 * 30 = 60 degrees.
XY is a diameter, so the upper half-circle X to Y is 180 degrees.
The arc from Z to X not through Y is the rest of that half-circle: 180 - 60 = 120 degrees.
Circumference = 2 * pi * 12 = 24*pi, so the arc length is (120/360) * 24*pi = 8*pi.
Check: arcs YZ (4*pi) + ZX (8*pi) = 12*pi = half the circumference.
medium.trap: Reading the 30-degree angle as the arc itself gives (30/360)(24*pi) = 2*pi (choice A); using the 60-degree arc YZ rather than the required arc gives 4*pi (choice B).

medium.question: Box A contains 2 red and 8 blue balls. Box B contains 6 red and 4 blue balls. A box is chosen randomly (each with probability 1/2) and one ball is drawn. The ball turns out to be red. What is the probability that it came from Box B?
medium.trap: Students compute P(red|Box B) = 6/10 = 3/5 and report that as the answer, reversing the direction of the conditional probability. Bayes' theorem is needed to find P(Box B | red).

medium.question: What is the slope of the line with equation 4x - 2y = 10?
medium.explanation: Convert to slope-intercept form: 4x - 2y = 10 → -2y = -4x + 10 → y = 2x - 5. The slope m = 2.
medium.trap: Students read the coefficient of x directly from standard form (4) as the slope without converting, choosing A.

medium.question: For x > 0, which of the following is equal to 3/√x?
medium.explanation: Multiply numerator and denominator by √x: (3 · √x) / (√x · √x) = 3√x / x. Note that x^(-1/2) = 1/√x, so 3/√x = 3x^(-1/2), but expressed with a rational denominator it is 3√x/x.
medium.trap: Multiplying only the denominator by √x without multiplying the numerator, getting 3/x.

medium.question: If a:b:c = 2:3:4, what is the value of (a^2 + b^2 + c^2)/(ab + bc + ca)?
medium.explanation:
Step 1 — every term on top and bottom is a product of two of the quantities, so the k^2 cancels and you can simply use a = 2, b = 3, c = 4.
Step 2 — numerator: 2^2 + 3^2 + 4^2 = 4 + 9 + 16 = 29.
Step 3 — denominator: ab + bc + ca = (2)(3) + (3)(4) + (4)(2) = 6 + 12 + 8 = 26.
Step 4 — the value is 29/26.
Formal check with the multiplier: numerator = 29k^2, denominator = 26k^2, and the k^2 divides out.
Answer: 29/26.
medium.trap: Miscounting the third product in the denominator. Writing ab twice - 6 + 12 + 6 = 24 - gives 29/24, choice C; the correct third term is ca = 4 x 2 = 8. The structural point is that top and bottom are both degree 2, so the multiplier cancels and you may substitute the bare ratio numbers 2, 3, 4.

medium.question: The first term of an infinite sequence is 9, and each term after the first is 6 greater than the preceding term. What is the 48th term of the sequence?
medium.explanation: In an arithmetic sequence the nth term equals the first term plus (n - 1) steps of the common difference. Here that gives 9 + (48 - 1) x 6 = 9 + 47 x 6 = 9 + 282 = 291.
medium.trap: Students multiply by 48 rather than 47 and answer 297. The 48th term sits only 47 steps past the first, because the first term itself takes no step.

medium.question: $200 is divided among A, B and C in the ratio 2:3:5. Which of the following amounts are among the three shares? Select all that apply.
medium.explanation:
Step 1 — name k. The shares are 2k, 3k and 5k.
Step 2 — the total is the invariant: 2k + 3k + 5k = 10k = 200, so k = 20.
Step 3 — the three shares are 2k = $40, 3k = $60 and 5k = $100.
A - $20 is k, the value of ONE ratio part, not anybody's share. FALSE.
B - $40 = 2k, A's share. TRUE.
C - $60 = 3k, B's share. TRUE.
D - $80 = 200 x 2/5, which uses the first and last ratio numbers as if the ratio were 2:5. FALSE.
E - $100 = 5k, C's share. TRUE.
Check: 40 + 60 + 100 = $200. Correct.
Answer: B, C, E.
medium.trap: Choice A is the value of one part and it is the most tempting wrong pick, because k is the number you just solved for. Choice D comes from dividing by 5 instead of by the sum of all three parts, 10 - with a three-part ratio the denominator is a + b + c, always.

medium.question: For a positive integer n, let f(n) be the sum of all positive divisors of n. For which of the following values of n is f(n) odd? Select all that apply.
medium.explanation:
The fast route: divisors pair as d and n/d, and the only divisors that are not cancelled out in parity are the odd ones. In fact f(n) is odd exactly when the ODD part of n is a perfect square, which means n is a perfect square or twice a perfect square. Compute each one to be certain.
A - n = 6: divisors 1, 2, 3, 6, sum = 12, even. (Odd part of 6 is 3, not a square.) FALSE.
B - n = 8: divisors 1, 2, 4, 8, sum = 15, odd. (8 = 2 x 4, twice a square; the only odd divisor is 1.) TRUE.
C - n = 12: divisors 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12, sum = 28, even. (Odd part 3, not a square.) FALSE.
D - n = 18: divisors 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18, sum = 39, odd. (18 = 2 x 9, twice a square.) TRUE.
E - n = 25: divisors 1, 5, 25, sum = 31, odd. (25 is a perfect square.) TRUE.
Check the pattern from a different angle: the odd divisors of 8 are just 1 (one of them, an odd count); of 18 they are 1, 3, 9 (three, odd count); of 25 they are 1, 5, 25 (three). The even divisors always pair off, so the parity of f(n) is the parity of the number of odd divisors - odd in exactly the three selected cases.
Answer: B, D, E.
medium.trap: Selecting A and C because 6 and 18 look alike (both are 2 x 3 x something) and 12 contains the square 4. What matters is the odd part alone: 18 = 2 x 3^2 has odd part 9, a square, while 6 = 2 x 3 and 12 = 2^2 x 3 have odd part 3, which is not. Rejecting B because 8 is 'very even' is the other slip: all of its even divisors cancel in parity and only the divisor 1 survives.

medium.question: What is the distance between points (0, 0) and (3, 4)?
medium.explanation: d = √((3−0)² + (4−0)²) = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5. This is the classic 3-4-5 Pythagorean triple.
medium.trap: Students may compute √(3 + 4) = √7 ≈ 2.65, forgetting to square each difference before adding. Always square first, then add, then take the root.

medium.question: A boutique shelf holds 8 different scarves, exactly 3 of which are wool. In how many different ways can 4 scarves be picked so that no more than one of the chosen scarves is wool?
medium.explanation:
1. Split by the number of wool scarves chosen: 0 or 1.
2. Zero wool: all 4 come from the 5 non-wool scarves, C(5,4) = 5 ways.
3. One wool: C(3,1) = 3 ways for the wool scarf and C(5,3) = 10 ways for the other three, 3*10 = 30 ways.
4. Total = 5 + 30 = 35.
Check by complement: C(8,4) = 70 total; two or more wool = C(3,2)*C(5,2) + C(3,3)*C(5,1) = 30 + 5 = 35; 70 - 35 = 35.
medium.trap: Counting only the exactly-one-wool case and forgetting the no-wool case gives 30.

hard.question:
a is a positive integer.

Quantity A: The greatest common divisor of a and a^2
Quantity B: a
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
hard.explanation: a divides a² (since a²=a×a), so a is a common divisor of a and a². Also, the greatest common divisor of a and a² ≤ a (since greatest common divisor divides a, and the largest divisor of a is a itself). Therefore the greatest common divisor of a and a² = a. The two quantities are always equal.
hard.trap: Students may think the greatest common divisor of a and a² could be a² (since a² is one of the numbers). But greatest common divisor must divide BOTH numbers, and a² does not divide a (for a>1). So greatest common divisor = a.

hard.question:
Parabola P: y = 2x² − 8x + 9

Quantity A: The y-coordinate of the vertex of P
Quantity B: The y-intercept of P
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
hard.explanation: Quantity A (vertex y-coordinate): Vertex x = −(−8)/(2×2) = 8/4 = 2. Vertex y = 2(2)² − 8(2) + 9 = 8 − 16 + 9 = 1. Quantity A = 1. Quantity B (y-intercept): set x = 0 → y = 9. Quantity B = 9. Since 1 < 9, Quantity B is greater.
hard.trap: Students confuse the vertex y-value with the y-intercept. The y-intercept is always c = 9 (the constant term). The vertex y-value requires substituting x = −b/(2a) = 2 back into the equation, giving 1.

hard.question:
a is a real constant, and the system (a - 1)x + 2y = 5 and 3x + (a + 1)y = 7 does NOT have exactly one solution.

Quantity A: a
Quantity B: 0
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
hard.explanation:
Step 1 — a two-by-two system has exactly one solution precisely when the x-ratio and the y-ratio differ, that is when (a - 1)/3 is not equal to 2/(a + 1). So 'not exactly one solution' means those ratios agree.
Step 2 — set them equal and cross-multiply: (a - 1)(a + 1) = 2 * 3, so a^2 - 1 = 6.
Step 3 — a^2 = 7, so a = sqrt(7) or a = -sqrt(7). Both are real, and both make the ratios agree, so both give a system with no solution or infinitely many - either way, not exactly one.
Step 4 — sqrt(7) is approximately 2.646, which is greater than 0, and -sqrt(7) is approximately -2.646, which is less than 0. The stem allows both, so Quantity A can be greater than Quantity B or less than it.
Check at a = sqrt(7): the system is (sqrt(7) - 1)x + 2y = 5 and 3x + (sqrt(7) + 1)y = 7. The x-ratio is (sqrt(7) - 1)/3, approximately 0.5486, and the y-ratio is 2/(sqrt(7) + 1) = 2(sqrt(7) - 1)/((sqrt(7) + 1)(sqrt(7) - 1)) = 2(sqrt(7) - 1)/6 = (sqrt(7) - 1)/3. The two ratios are identical, so the coefficient rows are proportional and the system does not have a unique solution. Correct. At a = -sqrt(7) the same cancellation gives (-sqrt(7) - 1)/3 = 2/(1 - sqrt(7)), again identical. Correct.
Answer: D.
hard.trap: Solving a^2 = 7 and keeping only the positive root sqrt(7), then comparing 2.646 with 0 and choosing A. The condition is quadratic in a, so it has two roots of opposite sign and the comparison cannot be settled. Choosing C comes from misreading a^2 - 1 = 6 as a - 1 = 6 or otherwise forcing a single value.

hard.question:
Line M: 2x - 3y = 12. Line N: slope = 2/3.

Quantity A: The slope of Line M
Quantity B: The slope of Line N
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
hard.explanation: Convert Line M: 2x - 3y = 12 → -3y = -2x + 12 → y = (2/3)x - 4. Slope of Line M = 2/3. Line N slope = 2/3. Both are equal.
hard.trap: Students read the slope of Line M directly from the standard form as 2 (coefficient of x) without converting, concluding Quantity A = 2 > 2/3.

hard.question:
x and y are real numbers with x > y > 0.
Quantity A: (x^3 - y^3) / (x - y)
Quantity B: (x + y)^2
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
hard.explanation:
Step 1 — factor the numerator of Quantity A: x^3 - y^3 = (x - y)(x^2 + xy + y^2). Since x > y, the factor x - y is nonzero and cancels.
Quantity A = x^2 + xy + y^2
Step 2 — expand Quantity B: (x + y)^2 = x^2 + 2xy + y^2.
Step 3 — subtract Quantity A from Quantity B:
(x^2 + 2xy + y^2) - (x^2 + xy + y^2) = xy
Step 4 — x > 0 and y > 0, so xy > 0. Quantity B exceeds Quantity A by xy, which is always positive here.
Check: put x = 3 and y = 1. Quantity A = (27 - 1)/2 = 13, and x^2 + xy + y^2 = 9 + 3 + 1 = 13. Quantity B = 16. Quantity B is greater, and the gap is xy = 3. Correct.
Answer: B.
hard.trap: Cancelling as if x^3 - y^3 factored like x^2 - y^2 and writing Quantity A as x^2 + 2xy + y^2, which makes the columns look equal and produces choice C. The quadratic factor of a difference of cubes has a single xy, not 2xy. Choosing D on the grounds that x and y are unknown also fails: the difference is xy, and the stem pins its sign by requiring x > y > 0.

hard.question: How many distinct orderings of the seven letters of ARRANGE, that is, of the multiset A, A, R, R, N, G, E, have the two A's NOT adjacent?
hard.explanation:
'Apart' is counted by complement: total minus together.
Step 1 — total orderings. Seven letters with A twice and R twice: 7!/(2! x 2!) = 5040/4 = 1260.
Step 2 — orderings with the two A's together, by the glue method. Treat AA as a single block, leaving 6 units: [AA], R, R, N, G, E. The R's are still repeated, so the count is 6!/2! = 720/2 = 360. There is no internal factor for the block, because the two A's are identical.
Step 3 — subtract: 1260 - 360 = 900.
Answer: 900.
hard.trap: Choice A, 360, is the 'together' count - the complement of what was asked. Choice D, 1260, is the unrestricted total. Choice E, 2520 = 7!/2!, divides out only one of the two repeated pairs. Choice B, 630 = 1260/2, assumes the A's are adjacent in half the orderings; adjacency requires two specific positions to be consecutive, which is far rarer than half.

hard.question: A 4 × 4 × 4 cube is painted red on all six faces and then cut into 64 unit cubes (each 1 × 1 × 1). How many unit cubes have exactly 2 red faces?
hard.explanation: Unit cubes with exactly 2 red faces lie along the edges of the original cube (but not at the corners). Each edge of a 4×4×4 cube has 4 unit cubes total; 2 are corner cubes (3 painted faces), leaving 2 edge cubes per edge with exactly 2 painted faces. A cube has 12 edges, so: 12 × 2 = 24 unit cubes with exactly 2 painted faces.
hard.trap: Students count corner cubes (which have 3 red faces = 8 cubes) and confuse them with edge cubes. The four categories: 8 corner cubes (3 faces), 24 edge cubes (2 faces), 24 face-center cubes (1 face), 8 interior cubes (0 faces). Total = 8+24+24+8 = 64 ✓.

hard.question: If f(x) = √x and g(x) = x - 3, what is the domain of f(g(x))?
hard.explanation:
First find the composite function: f(g(x)) = f(x - 3) = √(x - 3).
For the square root to be defined: x - 3 ≥ 0, so x ≥ 3.
hard.trap: Students use the domain of f(x) = √x alone (x ≥ 0) without substituting g(x), selecting A.

hard.question: Ray OB bisects angle AOC. Angle AOB = (4x + 7)° and angle BOC = (6x - 13)°. What is the measure of angle AOC?
hard.explanation: Since OB bisects angle AOC, angle AOB = angle BOC: 4x + 7 = 6x − 13 → 20 = 2x → x = 10. Then angle AOB = 47°, so angle AOC = 2 × 47° = 94°.
hard.trap: Students compute the half-angle (47°) and report it as the full angle AOC, choosing B.

hard.question: Two congruent 30-60-90 triangles are placed together along their hypotenuses to form a rectangle. If the hypotenuse of each triangle is 8, what is the area of the rectangle?
hard.explanation: A rectangle's diagonal splits it into two congruent right triangles, so joining two congruent 30-60-90 triangles along their common hypotenuse restores a rectangle whose sides are the two legs. With hypotenuse 8: short leg = 4, long leg = 4√3. Area = 4 × 4√3 = 16√3.
hard.trap: Students confuse which sides form the rectangle and compute area = short leg × hypotenuse = 4 × 8 = 32.

hard.question: What is the remainder when 2^10 is divided by 5?
hard.explanation:
Step 1 — build the cycle of powers of 2 on division by 5, reducing at every step:
2^1 = 2
2^2 = 4
2^3 = 8, which leaves 3
2^4 = 16, which leaves 1
2^5 leaves 2 again, so the cycle is (2, 4, 3, 1) and its length is 4.
Step 2 — locate the exponent: 10 = 4 x 2 + 2, so 10 leaves remainder 2 on division by 4.
Step 3 — take the 2nd entry of the cycle: 4.
Check: 2^10 = 1024 = 5 x 204 + 4. Correct.
Answer: 4.
hard.trap: Using a cycle length of 5 because there are 5 possible remainders, computing 10 leaves remainder 0 on division by 5, and landing on 1 (choice B). The length of the cycle is however many powers it takes to return to the start - here 4, not 5. Choice C is position 1 of the cycle and choice D is position 3, the two off-by-one slips on either side of the correct position 2; choice A is the belief that a power of 2 must eventually be divisible by 5.

hard.question: For which of the following values of n is (2 x 10^n)(5 x 10^(-4)) < 10^(-6)? Select all that apply.
hard.explanation:
Step 1 — simplify the left side once, in general. Coefficients: 2 x 5 = 10. Exponents: n + (-4) = n - 4.
(2 x 10^n)(5 x 10^(-4)) = 10 x 10^(n-4)
Step 2 — renormalise: the coefficient 10 is itself 10^1, so the product is 10^(n-4+1) = 10^(n-3).
Step 3 — the condition becomes 10^(n-3) < 10^(-6). Since 10^k grows with k, this is n - 3 < -6, i.e. n < -3.
Step 4 — test each option against n < -3:
A - n = -6 < -3. TRUE (value 10^(-9)).
B - n = -5 < -3. TRUE (value 10^(-8)).
C - n = -4 < -3. TRUE (value 10^(-7)).
D - n = -3 gives exactly 10^(-6), which is not LESS than 10^(-6). FALSE.
E - n = -2 gives 10^(-5), which is larger than 10^(-6). FALSE.
Answer: A, B, C.
hard.trap: The coefficients multiply to exactly 10, and a student who leaves the product as 10 x 10^(n-4) reads the exponent as n - 4 and solves n - 4 < -6, i.e. n < -2 - which wrongly admits D and E. D is the second trap on its own: at n = -3 the two sides are equal, and the inequality is strict, so equality does not qualify.

hard.question: a, b and c are positive integers and a^2 x b^3 x c is odd. Which of the following must be true? Select all that apply.
options: C. a + b + c is odd
D. a x b x c + 1 is odd
hard.explanation:
Step 1 — a product is odd only when every factor is odd. a^2 is odd only if a is odd, b^3 is odd only if b is odd, and c must be odd as well. So a, b and c are all odd.
A - a must be odd, as shown. TRUE.
B - odd + odd = even, so b + c is even. With b = 3, c = 5: 8. TRUE.
C - odd + odd = even, then even + odd = odd, so a + b + c is odd. With a = 3, b = 3, c = 5: 11. TRUE.
D - a x b x c is odd x odd x odd = odd, so a x b x c + 1 is even, not odd. With a = b = 1, c = 3: 3 + 1 = 4. FALSE.
E - an odd base to any power is odd, so a^b is odd. With a = 3, b = 3: 27. FALSE.
Check the whole set with a = 3, b = 5, c = 7: a^2 x b^3 x c = 9 x 125 x 7 = 7875, odd, as required. Then A holds, b + c = 12 even, a + b + c = 15 odd, abc + 1 = 105 + 1 = 106 even, a^b = 3^5 = 243 odd.
Answer: A, B, C.
hard.trap: Selecting D by computing that abc is odd and then reporting that value's parity instead of the parity after adding 1. Selecting E comes from assuming that a large exponent drags an odd base toward even; odd^n is odd for every n.

hard.question: What is 5 ÷ (2/3) ÷ (5/6)?
hard.trap: Students divide left to right without flipping correctly at each step, or flip both fractions simultaneously.

hard.question: A line passes through (-1, 2) and (3, -6). What is the y-intercept of this line?
hard.explanation:
Step 1 — Slope: m = (-6 - 2)/(3 - (-1)) = -8/4 = -2.
Step 2 — Use point-slope with (-1, 2): y - 2 = -2(x - (-1)) = -2(x + 1) → y - 2 = -2x - 2 → y = -2x - 2 + 2 = -2x.
The y-intercept is 0.
Verification: at x = 3: y = -2(3) = -6. ✓
hard.trap: Students write x - x1 = x - (-1) = x - 1 (dropping the double negative), giving y - 2 = -2(x - 1) → y = -2x + 2 + 2 = -2x + 4. They report y-intercept = 4.

questions.question:
A boat's speed in still water is 12 km/h. It travels 36 km upstream and 36 km downstream. The current's speed is c km/h, where 0 < c < 12.

Quantity A: Total time for the round trip (upstream + downstream)
Quantity B: 6 hours
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
questions.explanation: Upstream speed = 12 − c. Downstream speed = 12 + c. Time upstream = 36/(12 − c). Time downstream = 36/(12 + c). Total time = 36/(12−c) + 36/(12+c) = 36[(12+c) + (12−c)] / [(12−c)(12+c)] = 36(24) / (144−c²) = 864/(144−c²). When c = 0: total = 864/144 = 6 hours. For any c > 0: 144 − c² < 144, so 864/(144−c²) > 6. Since c > 0, Quantity A > 6 = Quantity B. Quantity A is always greater than Quantity B.
questions.trap: Students compute upstream time + downstream time as 36/12 + 36/12 = 3 + 3 = 6 hours, forgetting that the current alters the effective speeds, and choose C.

questions.question:
In the figure, triangle PQR is equilateral with each side equal to 6. Arc QSR is part of the circle with center P that passes through Q and R, and S is on the arc below chord QR.
Quantity A: The area of the region bounded by chord QR and arc QSR
Quantity B: 3
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
questions.explanation:
1. The arc is centered at P with radius PQ = 6, and angle QPR = 60 degrees (equilateral triangle).
2. The sector PQSR has area (60/360) * pi * 6^2 = 6*pi.
3. The triangle PQR has area (sqrt(3)/4) * 6^2 = 9*sqrt(3).
4. The region in Quantity A is the sector minus the triangle: 6*pi - 9*sqrt(3).
5. Numerically 6*pi is about 18.850 and 9*sqrt(3) is about 15.588, so the region is about 3.26, which is more than 3.
6. Safe bounds: 6*3.14 = 18.84 and 9*1.7321 = 15.589, giving 3.25 even with the pessimistic values. Quantity A is greater.
questions.trap: Rounding too coarsely, with pi as 3 and sqrt(3) as 1.7, gives 18 - 15.3 = 2.7, which seems to make Quantity B greater, choice B; the true value is only about 0.26 above 3, so the approximations must be tight.

questions.question:
Two chords AB and CD intersect inside a circle. AB = 12 and CD = 13. The chord AB is bisected at the intersection point.

Quantity A: The length of the longer segment of CD
Quantity B: 9
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
questions.explanation: By the intersecting-chords theorem, the product of AB's segments equals the product of CD's. AB is bisected, so each half = 6, giving 6 × 6 = 36. If CD's segments are x and 13 − x, then x(13 − x) = 36 → x² − 13x + 36 = 0 → x = 4 or 9. The longer segment is 9. Quantity A = 9 = Quantity B, so the quantities are equal.
questions.trap: Not applying the intersecting chords theorem and instead guessing the longer segment is half of CD = 6.5.

questions.question:
x is a negative number.
Quantity A: x
Quantity B: x^2
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — locate each column relative to zero. x is negative, so Quantity A < 0. A square of a non-zero number is positive, so Quantity B > 0.
Step 2 — anything negative is left of anything positive on the number line, so x < x^2 for EVERY negative x.
Step 3 — sample all of the negative territory to be sure:
x = -5: Quantity A = -5, Quantity B = 25. B greater.
x = -1: Quantity A = -1, Quantity B = 1. B greater.
x = -0.5: Quantity A = -0.5, Quantity B = 0.25. B greater.
x = -0.001: Quantity A = -0.001, Quantity B = 0.000001. B greater.
Quantity B is greater in every case.
Answer: B.
questions.trap: Choosing D because squaring behaves differently on x < -1 (it enlarges the magnitude) than on -1 < x < 0 (it shrinks it). That difference is real but irrelevant here: whatever the magnitude does, the sign flips to positive, and a positive always beats a negative. Never key D just because the magnitudes vary - check whether the ORDER varies.

questions.question:
M, p and q are positive numbers.
Quantity A: M(p^2 + q^2)/15
Quantity B: M(p + q)^2/15
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
questions.explanation: Both columns carry the same positive factor M/15, so the comparison reduces to p^2 + q^2 against (p + q)^2. Expanding the square gives (p + q)^2 = p^2 + 2pq + q^2, which exceeds p^2 + q^2 by exactly 2pq. Since p and q are both positive, 2pq is positive, so Quantity B is greater for every allowed choice of M, p and q.
questions.trap: Students recall that squaring a sum is not the sum of squares but cannot pin the direction, and answer 'cannot be determined'. The positivity of p and q fixes the sign of the 2pq gap, which settles it.

questions.question: In the figure, XY is a diameter of a circle whose radius is 12, and Z is a point on the circle above XY. The angle between chords XY and XZ at X measures 30 degrees. What is the length of the arc from Z to X that does not pass through Y?
questions.explanation:
Angle YXZ is an inscribed angle, so it is half of the arc it cuts off: arc YZ = 2 * 30 = 60 degrees.
XY is a diameter, so the upper half-circle X to Y is 180 degrees.
The arc from Z to X not through Y is the rest of that half-circle: 180 - 60 = 120 degrees.
Circumference = 2 * pi * 12 = 24*pi, so the arc length is (120/360) * 24*pi = 8*pi.
Check: arcs YZ (4*pi) + ZX (8*pi) = 12*pi = half the circumference.
questions.trap: Reading the 30-degree angle as the arc itself gives (30/360)(24*pi) = 2*pi (choice A); using the 60-degree arc YZ rather than the required arc gives 4*pi (choice B).

questions.question: Box A contains 2 red and 8 blue balls. Box B contains 6 red and 4 blue balls. A box is chosen randomly (each with probability 1/2) and one ball is drawn. The ball turns out to be red. What is the probability that it came from Box B?
questions.trap: Students compute P(red|Box B) = 6/10 = 3/5 and report that as the answer, reversing the direction of the conditional probability. Bayes' theorem is needed to find P(Box B | red).

questions.question: What is the slope of the line with equation 4x - 2y = 10?
questions.explanation: Convert to slope-intercept form: 4x - 2y = 10 → -2y = -4x + 10 → y = 2x - 5. The slope m = 2.
questions.trap: Students read the coefficient of x directly from standard form (4) as the slope without converting, choosing A.

questions.question: For x > 0, which of the following is equal to 3/√x?
questions.explanation: Multiply numerator and denominator by √x: (3 · √x) / (√x · √x) = 3√x / x. Note that x^(-1/2) = 1/√x, so 3/√x = 3x^(-1/2), but expressed with a rational denominator it is 3√x/x.
questions.trap: Multiplying only the denominator by √x without multiplying the numerator, getting 3/x.

questions.question: If a:b:c = 2:3:4, what is the value of (a^2 + b^2 + c^2)/(ab + bc + ca)?
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — every term on top and bottom is a product of two of the quantities, so the k^2 cancels and you can simply use a = 2, b = 3, c = 4.
Step 2 — numerator: 2^2 + 3^2 + 4^2 = 4 + 9 + 16 = 29.
Step 3 — denominator: ab + bc + ca = (2)(3) + (3)(4) + (4)(2) = 6 + 12 + 8 = 26.
Step 4 — the value is 29/26.
Formal check with the multiplier: numerator = 29k^2, denominator = 26k^2, and the k^2 divides out.
Answer: 29/26.
questions.trap: Miscounting the third product in the denominator. Writing ab twice - 6 + 12 + 6 = 24 - gives 29/24, choice C; the correct third term is ca = 4 x 2 = 8. The structural point is that top and bottom are both degree 2, so the multiplier cancels and you may substitute the bare ratio numbers 2, 3, 4.

questions.question: The first term of an infinite sequence is 9, and each term after the first is 6 greater than the preceding term. What is the 48th term of the sequence?
questions.explanation: In an arithmetic sequence the nth term equals the first term plus (n - 1) steps of the common difference. Here that gives 9 + (48 - 1) x 6 = 9 + 47 x 6 = 9 + 282 = 291.
questions.trap: Students multiply by 48 rather than 47 and answer 297. The 48th term sits only 47 steps past the first, because the first term itself takes no step.

questions.question: $200 is divided among A, B and C in the ratio 2:3:5. Which of the following amounts are among the three shares? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — name k. The shares are 2k, 3k and 5k.
Step 2 — the total is the invariant: 2k + 3k + 5k = 10k = 200, so k = 20.
Step 3 — the three shares are 2k = $40, 3k = $60 and 5k = $100.
A - $20 is k, the value of ONE ratio part, not anybody's share. FALSE.
B - $40 = 2k, A's share. TRUE.
C - $60 = 3k, B's share. TRUE.
D - $80 = 200 x 2/5, which uses the first and last ratio numbers as if the ratio were 2:5. FALSE.
E - $100 = 5k, C's share. TRUE.
Check: 40 + 60 + 100 = $200. Correct.
Answer: B, C, E.
questions.trap: Choice A is the value of one part and it is the most tempting wrong pick, because k is the number you just solved for. Choice D comes from dividing by 5 instead of by the sum of all three parts, 10 - with a three-part ratio the denominator is a + b + c, always.

questions.question: For a positive integer n, let f(n) be the sum of all positive divisors of n. For which of the following values of n is f(n) odd? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation:
The fast route: divisors pair as d and n/d, and the only divisors that are not cancelled out in parity are the odd ones. In fact f(n) is odd exactly when the ODD part of n is a perfect square, which means n is a perfect square or twice a perfect square. Compute each one to be certain.
A - n = 6: divisors 1, 2, 3, 6, sum = 12, even. (Odd part of 6 is 3, not a square.) FALSE.
B - n = 8: divisors 1, 2, 4, 8, sum = 15, odd. (8 = 2 x 4, twice a square; the only odd divisor is 1.) TRUE.
C - n = 12: divisors 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12, sum = 28, even. (Odd part 3, not a square.) FALSE.
D - n = 18: divisors 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18, sum = 39, odd. (18 = 2 x 9, twice a square.) TRUE.
E - n = 25: divisors 1, 5, 25, sum = 31, odd. (25 is a perfect square.) TRUE.
Check the pattern from a different angle: the odd divisors of 8 are just 1 (one of them, an odd count); of 18 they are 1, 3, 9 (three, odd count); of 25 they are 1, 5, 25 (three). The even divisors always pair off, so the parity of f(n) is the parity of the number of odd divisors - odd in exactly the three selected cases.
Answer: B, D, E.
questions.trap: Selecting A and C because 6 and 18 look alike (both are 2 x 3 x something) and 12 contains the square 4. What matters is the odd part alone: 18 = 2 x 3^2 has odd part 9, a square, while 6 = 2 x 3 and 12 = 2^2 x 3 have odd part 3, which is not. Rejecting B because 8 is 'very even' is the other slip: all of its even divisors cancel in parity and only the divisor 1 survives.

questions.question: What is the distance between points (0, 0) and (3, 4)?
questions.explanation: d = √((3−0)² + (4−0)²) = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5. This is the classic 3-4-5 Pythagorean triple.
questions.trap: Students may compute √(3 + 4) = √7 ≈ 2.65, forgetting to square each difference before adding. Always square first, then add, then take the root.

questions.question: A boutique shelf holds 8 different scarves, exactly 3 of which are wool. In how many different ways can 4 scarves be picked so that no more than one of the chosen scarves is wool?
questions.explanation:
1. Split by the number of wool scarves chosen: 0 or 1.
2. Zero wool: all 4 come from the 5 non-wool scarves, C(5,4) = 5 ways.
3. One wool: C(3,1) = 3 ways for the wool scarf and C(5,3) = 10 ways for the other three, 3*10 = 30 ways.
4. Total = 5 + 30 = 35.
Check by complement: C(8,4) = 70 total; two or more wool = C(3,2)*C(5,2) + C(3,3)*C(5,1) = 30 + 5 = 35; 70 - 35 = 35.
questions.trap: Counting only the exactly-one-wool case and forgetting the no-wool case gives 30.
